task: F2 robustness/security audit of world-model physics instrumentation
originalIntent: Ship opt-in physics_capture_v1 collection whose synchronized PNG/state/event artifacts are bounded, validated, atomically promoted, quarantined on invalid completion, and safe to resume without weakening legacy capture behavior.
desiredOutcome: A caller can collect or validate enriched shots without accepting artifacts outside the shot root, exhausting memory on oversized sidecars, or failing/leaving a new partial attempt when collection is resumed over an already valid final shot.
userOutcomeReview: The normal one-shot path works and the focused suites are deterministic, but the shipped artifact does not satisfy the requested robustness outcome. Fresh real-surface probes accepted an escaped sidecar and failed a repeated resume with ENOTEMPTY while leaving shot_001.tmp. Direct source inspection also proves validation materializes complete untrusted sidecars and hashes via whole-file reads before/after enforcing declared limits.

criteria.F2-BOUNDED-MEMORY: .omo/plans/world-model-physics-instrumentation.md:168-169 requires bounded-memory behavior; Todo 5 lines 116-120 requires streamed sidecars and malformed/truncated exclusion.
criteria.T5-ATOMIC-RESUME: .omo/plans/world-model-physics-instrumentation.md:116-120 requires atomic tmp-to-final promotion, invalid-completed quarantine, and remove/ignore incomplete tmp directories on resume.
criteria.F2-PATH-ROOT-PROTECTION: F2 robustness/security review requires path/root protections; canonical validation must not consume artifacts outside the accepted shot root.
criteria.T5-ACCEPTANCE: .omo/plans/world-model-physics-instrumentation.md:120-121 names the focused persistence/validation suites and corrupt/interrupted cases.

findings.observation: The JSONL boundary uses Path.read_text().splitlines(), materializing the entire untrusted sidecar before record/byte limits are checked. Artifact hashing additionally uses read_bytes() for every PNG and both sidecars. Declared max_total_bytes is validated only after parsing, so it is not a parser/memory bound.
findings.binaryObservable: Direct source calls Path.read_text and Path.read_bytes on the complete files; no bounded reader or pre-read stat/byte ceiling exists on this path.

findings.observation: validate_rollout_artifact accepted a physics_state.jsonl symlink whose target was outside shot_001. The physics validator opens fixed sidecar paths directly and never applies the canonical _artifact_rejection symlink/root checks to the sidecars.

Recovery validates an existing final shot but collection restarts at shot_001; promotion then calls Path.replace onto the existing nonempty directory. The real collector raised ENOTEMPTY and left a fresh shot_001.tmp, so cancel/resume is not idempotent or interruption-safe.
findings.binaryObservable: repeated_resume_exception=OSError; errno 39 Directory not empty; tmp_attempt_after_resume=true; final_attempt_after_resume=true

notes.observation: The focused tests pass twice but cover only first promotion and deletion of handcrafted tmp directories; they do not repeat collection over a valid final shot or test sidecar symlink escape. This creates misleading confidence rather than tautological failure-only coverage.

Direct remove-ai-slops/programming pass found oversized changed modules (physics_capture_parsing.py 295 lines, rollout_artifacts.py 354 lines, collect_rollouts.py 2128 lines) and a 3105-line collector test module. This is maintenance burden, but the rejection is based on the reproduced criterion failures above, not size alone.
notes.evidencePointer: wc output captured during audit; scripts/physics_capture_parsing.py; scripts/rollout_artifacts.py; scripts/collect_rollouts.py; tests/test_collect_rollouts.py

notes.observation: The persistence writer streams sidecar hashes/counts and fsyncs sidecars, uses frozen slotted records, validates deterministic state/event ordering, rejects event/byte overflow, and writes only under the supplied output directory in the normal path.
